title: Monitor how real users experience your app

blocks.content: Set up two views of your website: Synthetic Monitoring checks availability from outside your network, and Frontend Observability collects real user performance and errors from the browser.

blocks.prompt: Enter your website origin, such as https://yourcompany.com. Both setups use it.

blocks.content: First, point an uptime check at {{appUrl}}. You need the Editor or Admin role.
Open **Synthetic Monitoring**.
blocks.tooltip: Open the setup page in this Grafana instance.

whenTrue.content: Click **Get started** if this stack has not used Synthetic Monitoring before. Ask an administrator to complete this one-time setup.
whenTrue.tooltip: An administrator only needs to initialize this service once per stack.

blocks.content: Open a new **API Endpoint** check. It starts as an HTTP check, which requests your page the way a browser would.
blocks.tooltip: Open the setup page in this Grafana instance.

blocks.content: Enter a descriptive **Job name**, such as `my-website-uptime`.
blocks.formHint: Enter a descriptive name for your application or check.
blocks.tooltip: This name becomes the job label used to find the check in metrics and logs.

blocks.content: Set **Request target** to {{appUrl}}.
blocks.tooltip: An HTTP check requests this URL; it does not execute JavaScript or simulate a complete browser session.

blocks.content: Click **Execution** to choose probe locations and a schedule.
blocks.tooltip: Each selected location runs the check independently at the frequency you choose.

blocks.content: Select at least one online probe near your users. Review **Frequency** and the estimated usage before saving; more probes and more frequent checks generate more usage.
Click **Save** to start the check and open its dashboard.
blocks.tooltip: Review the target, selected probes, and estimated usage before saving.

blocks.content: Probes are now testing {{appUrl}} from outside your network, around the clock.
Next, create a Frontend Observability application that accepts data from the same URL:
Open **Connect your web application** in **Frontend Observability**.
blocks.tooltip: Open the setup page in this Grafana instance.

blocks.content: Enter your own **Application name**, such as `my-web-app`.
blocks.formHint: Enter a descriptive name for your application or check.
blocks.tooltip: Use a name that distinguishes this frontend from other applications and environments.

blocks.content: Set **Allowed origins** to {{appUrl}}.
blocks.tooltip: Use the scheme, hostname, and port your visitors use; add other environments separately.

blocks.content: Click **Next** to create the application and its collector endpoint.
blocks.tooltip: Creating the application does not send browser data; you must still install and deploy Faro.

blocks.content: Your application exists and is waiting for its first data.
Finally, copy the Faro snippet that sends real user data from {{appUrl}}:
Choose **Manual instrumentation** to view the SDK installation instructions.
blocks.tooltip: The other options can help modify your codebase; manual setup lets you choose how to install the SDK.

blocks.content: Click **Copy** and follow the instructions for your chosen installation method in your application.
blocks.tooltip: Initialize Faro early so it can capture errors during page startup; deploy the change before checking for data.

blocks.content: Once you deploy the snippet, sessions, errors, and Web Vitals from real users start arriving.
After deploying Faro, you can compare availability checks with real user sessions and errors for {{appUrl}}. Source maps and alert rules are optional and can be configured later.
